summary: Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3) turned bin.ts into a thin dispatcher. Its only static imports are compileCache.ts (node:module) and the dependency-free stdioProxyProtocol.ts. The device host, Agent Control stdio proxy, external MCP bridge and cliMain are each loaded via dynamic import() after the argv check, so neither helper mode evaluates the server graph any more. The built dist keeps this: bin.mjs's static closure is just itself (3 KB), and the proxy's is 3 chunks (~10 KB). Running `node dist/bin.mjs __agent-control-stdio-proxy` end to end takes 0.03 s, the same as bare `node -e 0`. The external bridge is ~93% fixed against the finding's 665 ms. Its closure is still 8 chunks / ~700 KB: effect core plus the contracts agentControl/auth/settings/server/orchestration schemas, all pulled in because ExternalMcp/runtimeFiles.ts imports the @ryco/contracts barrel for a single string constant. Measured costs for the bridge closure are ~40 ms uncached / ~30 ms cached with +30 MB RSS (40 to 70 MB) on Node 24, and ~29 ms with +26 MB RSS (60 to 86 MB) in packaged Ryco Electron node mode. For comparison, the full cliMain graph today costs ~100-135 ms and +70 MB. That RSS is held for the whole life of each bridge process, i.e. per external MCP client session. The serverBundleBoundaries test guards the closures of bin.ts and stdioProxy.ts but not bridge.ts. That residual is a small follow-up, not a reason to reopen. No functional regressions found. CursorAdapter is the only stdio-proxy caller and ProviderInjection still passes [argv1, proxy arg]. The externalSetup bridge args match bin.ts's fast-path parser exactly. The CLI has no other `mcp` subcommand that could fall through to cliMain. The rolldown stdioProxy-chunk -> ./bin.mjs edge resolves to the already-evaluated entry, the same pattern cliMain already relies on.

evidence.note: Only static imports: stdioProxyProtocol.ts and compileCache.ts. The header comment (lines 1-9) states the intent.

enableCompileCacheBestEffort, then dispatch via dynamic import(): device-host-stdio, AGENT_CONTROL_STDIO_PROXY_ARG -> ./agentControl/stdioProxy.ts, mcp pair|serve -> ./agentControl/ExternalMcp/bridge.ts, else ./cliMain.ts.
Imports only node:readline, Mcp/jsonRpc.ts, Mcp/transportGuard.ts (constants) and stdioProxyProtocol.ts.

Residual: `import { AGENT_CONTROL_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE } from "@ryco/contracts"` (used as a value at :189 and a type at :19). This pulls the contracts barrel plus effect into the bridge closure. The built runtimeFiles-*.mjs chunk is 142 KB of contracts regions and imports device-*.mjs (411 KB, effect core) and orchestration-*.mjs (110 KB).
The constant is just `"external-mcp" as const`.
bridge.ts already hardcodes the literal "external-mcp" (also at :80), so hoisting the constant is trivial.
Regression guards exist for the bin.ts closure (exact file list) and the stdioProxy.ts closure (<10 files, no packages/). There is no equivalent guard for ExternalMcp/bridge.ts.
Still a single entry, src/bin.ts. The proposal's dedicated tsdown entries were not added; dynamic-import dispatch gives the same isolation.
Built dispatcher keeps the import() boundaries. Measured closures: bin.mjs 1 chunk/3 KB; stdioProxy 3 chunks/10 KB; bridge 8 chunks/699 KB; cliMain 49 chunks/6.46 MB.
The only stdio-proxy caller: execPath + argv[1] (bin.mjs), now cheap.
The proxy mcpServer is still [proxyEntryPoint, AGENT_CONTROL_STDIO_PROXY_ARG], which matches the bin.ts fast path.
Installed bridge args [entry, mcp, pair|serve, --integration, id, --state-dir, dir] match bin.ts externalMcpArgs(). New Electron configs also set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 (:51,:60).
Packaged legacy configs that launch Electron without RUN_AS_NODE are forwarded headless to a node-mode bridge before any GUI services load.

fixDefects: No functional defect. One small uncovered part: the external MCP bridge path (`bin.mjs mcp serve|pair`) still loads ~700 KB / 8 chunks (effect core plus contracts agentControl/auth/settings/server/orchestration schemas). The cause is apps/server/src/agentControl/ExternalMcp/runtimeFiles.ts:5 importing the @ryco/contracts barrel for one string constant. Measured costs are ~30-40 ms of import time and +26-30 MB RSS per bridge process, against ~0.4 ms / +0 MB for the lean proxy closure. The bridge is long-lived (one per external MCP client session), so that RSS is held, not transient. Nothing guards the bridge closure: serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts:125-139 covers only bin.ts and stdioProxy.ts.
implementationSketch: Optional follow-up, low priority. (1) Add apps/server/src/agentControl/ExternalMcp/externalMcpProtocol.ts, a dependency-free module like stdioProxyProtocol.ts: `export const EXTERNAL_MCP_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE = "external-mcp" as const;`. Add a compile-time equality check against contracts using only a type import (erased): `import type { AGENT_CONTROL_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE } from "@ryco/contracts"` plus a `satisfies`/conditional-type assertion that the two literal types are equal. Alternatively, expose a constants-only contracts subpath (contracts already uses subpath exports, e.g. ./settings, ./relay). (2) In runtimeFiles.ts, swap the value import at :5 for the new constant (type at :19, check at :189). In bridge.ts:71/:80, use it in place of the literals. (3) Extend serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts with `it("loads the external MCP bridge without the server graph")`: assert staticGraph("src/agentControl/ExternalMcp/bridge.ts") has <10 files and none under packages/. Also, in the built-bundle describe, resolve the bridge chunk from bin.mjs's `import("./bridge-...")` and assert that its builtStaticClosure contains no `//#region ../../node_modules/.bun/effect` and totals under ~50 KB. (4) Verify by rebuilding the server: the bridge closure should drop from ~700 KB to a few KB, and `node --input-type=module -e "await import('<dist>/bridge-*.mjs')"` should take <1 ms with RSS near the bare-node baseline. Run only the focused server tests (bun run test on serverBundleBoundaries, ExternalMcp/bridge.test.ts, runtimeFiles tests).
decisionReason: Not needed. The core fix is done, and the optional follow-up only moves a string constant used in the external credential-file audience check without changing its value or semantics. No auth, E2EE, Hub or hosted-lifecycle decisions are involved.
